nodes.plm_action: Threading hearts together with string
nodes.plm_caption: This video features two hands, that decorate paper hearts with nail polishes and paint them.  Also part of the hands are two more items being prepared and painted in red.  There are 3 paper hearts on the table. The video ends with the hands on the "About" page.

summary.brief: The creator bends wire into heart shapes, paints and glitters them, shows three finished heart‑photo holders, and ends on the channel’s About page.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the creator drawing two heart outlines on paper as templates. Using a nail‑polish cap as a round guide and pliers, wire is bent around the first template to form a heart, then the process is repeated to make a second heart and a small bottom curl. Each wire heart is painted with nail polish (usually pink) and, after the paint dries, a layer of glitter is applied. Three finished heart photo holders are displayed—one plain, one painted, and one sparkling—and each is shown in a different size on a stand made from coiled wire. The creator then decorates nearby boxes, jars, marbles and base cups with the hearts for additional styling. A montage of gift‑box, teddy‑bear and other Valentine‑themed items follows, and the video concludes with a screen of the channel’s About page and a call to subscribe.

action.detailed: Use pliers and a nail‑polish cap to bend wire around the drawn heart templates, then paint the shaped wires with nail polish, coat them with glitter, and arrange the finished hearts as decorative photo holders.

nodes.plm_action: Hold heart-shaped wire frame in place using pliers

The video features a collection of different images which alternate in a timeline. These photos display images of nature and people, and also contain some text. The main video section begins at 1s and shows the hands of someone creating a wire heart decoration. That section is also timelined. The hands are shown creating the decoration with a pen, pliers and some additional materials to coat it in a pink glittery paint. In the second part of the video the music stops and it transitions to a background with the words "My Sparkle DIY" and a logo of a heart.
The person's hands appear to be the only element in the video which interacts with their environment and the environment changes frequently. At times the person is using various tools like pliers and a pencil to manipulate the wire heart in their hand and the wire heart is the only object which is created during the second half of the video.
The hand of the person, and the wire heart are the only elements in the environment which are manipulating the environment. The hands are in constant motion, which is important in order for the video to be successful.
Lightning strikes, a collection of different images flashing across the timeline, a music video. There are four main elements in the video, the photos and the music video, and the hands of the person.
The videos runs for 22 seconds. The photos are played for 5 seconds, the music video runs for 17 seconds and the hands of the person runs for 0 seconds.

summary.brief: A DIY video shows hands drawing, bending wire into hearts, painting and glittering them to create decorative photo‑holder decorations.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a rapid montage of heart‑themed photos, subscribe graphics and a "My Sparkle DIY" logo. The view then switches to a close‑up of a pair of hands at a white work surface. The maker sketches two heart outlines on paper, cuts a length of thin metal wire, and uses pliers together with a nail‑polish cap as a round guide to bend the wire around the drawn shape, forming a heart. The same procedure is repeated to create a second heart, and the wire is bent at the bottom to form a small loop that can hold a photo. After the wire shapes are finished, pink nail polish is applied to the hearts; while the polish is still wet, pink glitter is sprinkled over the surfaces and allowed to dry. The finished hearts are displayed in three variations—a plain painted version, a glitter‑sparkled version, and a smaller stand‑type version—showing the completed wire‑heart photo holders.

action.detailed: Draw heart outlines on paper, cut and bend wire with pliers and a nail‑polish cap to match the outlines, form a loop at the bottom, paint the wire hearts with pink nail polish, sprinkle pink glitter onto the wet paint, let it dry, and present the completed decorative holders.

summary.brief: Hands shape, paint and glitter wire hearts to create decorative photo‑holder pieces.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with the creator’s hands drawing heart outlines on white paper, then cutting short lengths of thin metal wire and inserting the pieces into a nail‑polish bottle cap to hold them. Using round‑nose pliers the wire is bent, trimmed and formed into small heart shapes. The newly formed wire hearts are coated with pink or red nail polish, allowed to dry, and sometimes secured with tiny clothespins. After the paint dries, the hearts are dusted or brushed with matching glitter, producing sparkling decorations. Throughout the sequence the hands repeatedly reposition the hearts, apply paint, add glitter, and display each finished piece. Near the end the hands show a nail file, glue, and three glitter‑covered wire hearts that are ready to be used as decorative photo‑holder ornaments.

summary.brief: Hands draw heart outlines, cut and bend wire into heart shapes, and coat the wire hearts with nail polish.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a pair of hands working over a white surface. A blue sketch pen is used to draw simple heart outlines on a sheet of paper. A thin piece of silver wire is then cut to length with small pliers. The wire is placed on the paper and, using the pliers, the ends are bent and curved repeatedly until a clear heart silhouette is formed; excess wire is trimmed as needed. Occasionally a paperclip or small plastic piece is wrapped with the wire to help define the shape. Once the wire heart is complete, it is dipped or brushed with nail polish from a nearby bottle (pink or red in color), giving the wire a glossy coated finish. The painted heart is held up for the camera, and the process is repeated to create a second heart before the segment ends.

action.brief: Shape and paint a wire heart
action.detailed: Cut a length of thin wire with pliers, bend and curve the wire with the pliers until it forms a heart shape, trim any excess, then dip or brush the wire heart with nail polish and present the finished painted heart.

   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*

   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)
